title: PermissionRequested
description: The one `request` that travels server to client, and the reason the whole protocol is a socket instead of a stream: `canUseTool` has blocked the agent loop and it stays blocked until somebody answers or the deadline passes. Answered with the `permission.resolve` response.

requestId.description: Idempotency is by **this** field, never by `toolUseId`.

toolUseId.description: The invocation this request is about, tying it to the `tool.started` already on screen.

title.description: Short label of what is being asked, derived by the backend.

description.description: The detail a human needs to decide — the command line, the path being written.

input.description: The exact input the tool would run with. What is shown is what executes.

riskHint.description: Derived in the backend, by a per-tool list **plus** a heuristic over the input, and it fails closed: a command the heuristic does not recognise is marked `destructive`. A false positive is an annoyance; a false negative is the accident.

defaultToNo.description: The UI pre-selects refusal. Silence never authorises.

expiresAt.description: When the request is denied automatically, ISO 8601 in UTC. Ours is the only timeout there is — the CLI imposes none.

suggestions.description: Scopes the UI may offer beyond a one-off yes. `project` and `always` come whenever the request has at least one reach in `reaches` (and `project` only with a workspace).

labelKey.description: An i18n key. The server never sends prose.

pattern.description: What a rule granted with the `exact` reach would match, in the grammar of the Claude Code settings. Kept for clients that do not read `reaches`; absent when there is no `exact` reach.

lifetimeMs.description: How long a rule granted by this suggestion would live, counted from the answer. Present on `project` and `always`; the number is the installation's, never the client's.

reaches.description: How far a rule left by this answer may reach, computed by the server from the invocation. The client picks one and answers with its `reach`, never with a pattern: the server computes the patterns again and refuses a reach it did not offer. Applies to `session`, `project` and `always`.

reach.description: `exact` is this very input; `prefix` (shell only) covers every command that starts like each command of this line; `tool` (never shell) is every invocation of the tool.

patterns.description: The rules this reach would leave, one per pattern, in the grammar of the Claude Code settings. Shown in full before anybody confirms.
